items.title: When simulations fall short, this spectrometer learns for itself
items.excerpt: Aarhus University researchers used AI to let an NMR spectrometer learn the best pulse sequence directly from the sample, instead of relying on simulations, to boost weak signals that limit what the instrument can see.
items.rationale: Fresh (10-28) method result in which AI tunes a lab instrument in place, on the sample itself. It moves 'AI for science' from analysing data to running the experiment.

items.title: Pasqal Launches AI Workflow for Cloud Quantum Experiments
items.excerpt: Pasqal's new AI-driven cloud workflow prepares quantum jobs, validates them in emulation, and processes the results into scientific observables.
items.rationale: New product release (10-28): an end-to-end AI workflow that takes cloud quantum experiments from job prep through emulation to observables. It is a different event from the Google competition published 10-24.

items.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel?
items.excerpt: Ai2's Old Ideas, Novel Problems benchmark tests how reliably LLMs judge the novelty of research ideas and finds small changes to the evaluation setup can flip their verdicts.
items.rationale: Primary-source benchmark release from Ai2 showing that LLM novelty verdicts flip under small setup changes. This matters directly to anyone using LLMs for research triage or review.

items.title: Rice plants can fight off devastating disease after gene editing with AI-designed tool
items.excerpt: University of Missouri researchers used an AI-designed genome-editing tool to create rice plants that resist bacterial blight, a disease that can destroy harvests across Asia and Africa.
items.rationale: Applied plant-science result: an AI-designed editor gives crops resistance to bacterial blight. It is host-side defence with no pathogen engineering, and it is not clinical, so it belongs in science.

items.title: AI may quickly generate ideas, but working with people leads to more creative ones
items.excerpt: A study comparing idea generation with generative AI versus human collaboration finds AI is faster but people working together produce more creative ideas.
items.rationale: New cognitive-science study (10-28) on AI versus human collaboration in ideation. It covers the psychology axis of the section and gives a practical takeaway for creative teams.
